title: Decision Trees (CART)
subtitle: Recursive Orthogonal Splits & Gini Impurity
summary: Partition feature space with axis-aligned splits maximizing Gini Impurity reduction.

evaluationChart.title: Feature Importance (Gini Gain)
evaluationChart.description: Shows the total normalized Gini impurity reduction contributed by Feature x₁ vs. Feature x₂.

advantages: White-box interpretability: decisions map directly to human-readable if/else rules.
Requires zero feature scaling or normalization.
Naturally handles non-linear interactions and mixed data types.
limitations: High variance: small data perturbations can produce a completely different tree.
Prone to overfitting deep branches without max_depth pruning.
Axis-aligned splits struggle with diagonal linear boundaries.
applications: Base learner for Random Forests & XGBoost

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

def gini(y):
    if len(y) == 0: return 0.0
    _, counts = np.unique(y, return_counts=True)
    p = counts / len(y)
    return 1.0 - np.sum(p ** 2)

print('Impurity of [0,0,1,1]:', gini(np.array([0, 0, 1, 1])))
codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier, export_text
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1.5,2.0],[1.9,6.8],[6.2,2.5],[6.8,6.9]])
y = np.array([0, 1, 1, 0])

tree = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=2, random_state=42).fit(X, y)
print(export_text(tree, feature_names=['x1', 'x2']))
print('Feature importances:', tree.feature_importances_)
